# ASAM specification references — master index

Local Markdown copies of the ASAM standards RoadMaker implements, tracked so
every checkout and worktree has them. Generated by
`scripts/fetch_asam_specs.py` — never hand-edited.

**Rights, licence, and why OpenSCENARIO is absent: [README.md](README.md).**
These copies are converted from the published HTML and are **non-normative** —
for anything you intend to rely on, read the source URL in the file header.

## Contents

| Directory | Spec | Version | Chapters | Size | Fetched |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opendrive-1.8.1/` | ASAM OpenDRIVE | 1.8.1 | 20 | 848 KB | 2026-07-25 |
| `opendrive-1.9.0/` | ASAM OpenDRIVE | 1.9.0 | 20 | 996 KB | 2026-07-25 |

Start at each directory's `INDEX.md` (chapter map + topic→file lookup).

**Both versions are kept on purpose.** RoadMaker targets 1.8.1 and 1.9.0, and
where they differ the difference must be handled explicitly and tested, with a
code comment citing both chapters — so the two texts sit side by side to be
diffed. Directory names always carry the concrete version, never "latest".

## Not tracked

| Spec | Version | Why |
|---|---|---|
| ASAM OpenSCENARIO XML | 1.4.0 | no redistribution grant — see [README](README.md#asam-openscenario-not-tracked) |

Fetch it locally when P8 work needs it:

```sh
python scripts/fetch_asam_specs.py --std openscenario --out third_party/asam
```

It lands beside these directories and is gitignored.

## Regenerating

```sh
python -m venv /tmp/asam-fetch-venv
/tmp/asam-fetch-venv/bin/pip install requests beautifulsoup4 markdownify
/tmp/asam-fetch-venv/bin/python scripts/fetch_asam_specs.py \
    --std opendrive --out third_party/asam
```

Requests are throttled and the script is the only supported way to change these
files. A refresh that changes a chapter RoadMaker cites should be reviewed like
any other diff — a specification erratum can invalidate a validator rule.

## Out of scope

ASAM OpenSCENARIO DSL 2.x, ASAM OpenCRG and other ASAM standards are
intentionally not fetched; add them when their pillars arrive, and check each
one's licence separately — the OpenDRIVE grant does **not** generalize.
